Unlike its sibling [Axis-Aligned Sheet-Buffered Splatting](5593-axis-aligned-sheet-buffered-splatting.md), which organizes voxels into fixed volume slices parallel to the viewing axis, image-aligned splatting advances a slab across the volume, slicing and projecting all intersecting kernels into sheet buffers [S2, unofficial][S4, book].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in both Source [S2] and Source [S4]. Both sources describe 'image-aligned splatting' (also referred to as image-aligned sheet-buffered splatting) as a method that advances a slab across the volume, slicing and projecting intersecting kernels into sheet buffers. They also contrast this with 'axis-aligned sheet-buffered splatting,' noting that the latter organizes voxels into fixed volume slices parallel to the viewing axis, which leads to popping artifacts when the view direction changes. The claim correctly identifies these operational differences and the associated artifacts/costs as described in the evidence.
